data.verdict: The best rate we could check is at Mamy Exchange in Koh Kaew, on route 402 between the airport and Phuket Town. On 15 Oct 2026 it paid 33.35 THB per USD 100 note and 37.35 THB per euro, about 0.5% under the mid-market rate. In Patong, use Lion in Jungceylon. In Old Town, use the SuperRich partner at Suriyadej Circle (closed Sundays). Bank booths paid 0.4-1.2% less. ATMs charge 250 THB (Visa) or 350 THB (Mastercard) per withdrawal, so bring clean USD or EUR notes.

atm.feeText: In 2026 Thai bank ATMs charge foreign cards 250 THB per withdrawal with Visa or UnionPay and 350 THB with Mastercard (official fee tables: Kasikorn from 25 Aug 2026, SCB from 1 Sep 2026, Krungsri from 11 Mar 2026). Your home bank may add a fee. One withdrawal is usually 20,000-30,000 THB at most.
cheapest: We found no cheaper bank ATM: Kasikorn, SCB and Krungsri all charge 250 THB (Visa) or 350 THB (Mastercard). A 2026 guide says Bangkok Bank and Krungthai also charge 250 THB.
Use a Visa card if you have one. It saves 100 THB on each withdrawal.
Take out the maximum each time (20,000-30,000 THB). A 250 THB fee is 1.25% of 20,000 THB but 5% of 5,000 THB.
Use ATMs at bank branches or inside malls (Jungceylon, Central Festival). If the machine keeps your card, the bank can help.
tips: If the ATM offers to convert to your home currency, press 'Decline' or 'Without conversion'. Your own bank then converts at a better rate.
Check the fee on the screen before you press OK.
Wise and Revolut cards do not remove the Thai ATM fee of 250/350 THB.
Standalone ATMs in bars and small shops can have lower withdrawal limits.
Withdraw in daylight, cover your PIN, and keep your cash in two places.

cards: Always pay in THB. If a card machine offers your home currency (DCC), say no. On 15 Oct 2026 SCB's card DCC rate was 31.85 THB per USD, while the mid-market rate was 33.50. That is about 5% worse.
Wise and Revolut cards convert close to the mid-market rate. Use them in malls, hotels, for Grab and for bigger bills.
Revolut: do big exchanges on weekdays. Standard plans add about 1% at weekends. Check the free monthly limit of your plan.
You still need cash for taxis, tuk-tuks, markets, beach bars and many small shops. Some places add a fee (often about 3%) for card payments.
Bring two cards from different banks, ideally one Visa and one Mastercard. Keep one card in the hotel safe.
Turn on foreign use in your banking app before you fly.
tips: Best plan: bring clean USD 100 or EUR 100/200 notes and change them at Mamy, Lion or the SuperRich partner. Use ATMs only as a backup.
Big notes get better rates. At Mamy on 15 Oct 2026: USD 50-100 notes 33.35, USD 5-20 notes 33.05 and USD 1-2 notes 32.55 THB.
Notes must be clean: not torn, not written on and not stamped. Old USD 100s get less: on 15 Oct 2026 Ex24 paid 33.08 for old 100s and 33.18 for new ones. Very old or damaged notes can be refused.
Bring your original passport. Changers ask for it and write down the number. Count the baht at the counter and keep the receipt.

Test a rate quickly: for USD 100 notes a good rate is within about 0.5% of the mid-market rate. On 15 Oct 2026 Mamy paid 33.35 when the mid-market rate was 33.50. A booth that pays 33.00 or less is about 1.5% under the mid-market rate.
For USD 1,000 on 15 Oct 2026 you got 33,350 THB at Mamy, 33,220 THB at the ttb bank, 33,070 THB at the SCB bank, and only about 31,850 THB when you paid by card with DCC.

When you arrive, change only a little at the airport or use an ATM there. Mamy is on Thepkrasattri Rd (route 402), on the way from the airport to Phuket Town and Patong. Ask your driver to stop (open Mon-Fri until 17:00, at weekends until 16:30).
In Patong, use Lion in Jungceylon (09:00-21:00). Late at night, the Value Plus booth on Soi Sansabai is open until 04:00.
In Phuket Old Town, use the SuperRich partner at Suriyadej Circle (Mon-Sat 10:00-20:00) or NC Plus (Mon-Sat). Both are closed on Sunday, and 10 Jan and 17 Jan 2027 are Sundays.
In Kata/Karon, Rawai/Nai Harn and Bang Tao/Laguna, use Money Shop, Value Plus or a bank booth. Before you change a big amount, compare with Mamy's live rate on mamyexchange.com.
Natai and Khao Pilai (Phang Nga) have almost no money changers (OpenStreetMap shows none). Bring baht from Phuket.

Green SuperRich Thailand and Vasu Exchange have no Phuket branch: green SuperRich lists only Bangkok and nearby cities, and Vasu has one Bangkok office. The Google pin 'Superrich Money Exchange' on Wirat Hong Yok Rd is not SuperRich: the company there is registered as 'Sunrich Money Exchange'.
On 15 Oct 2026 SuperRich in Bangkok paid 33.43-33.45 for a USD 100 note. Mamy in Phuket paid only about 0.1 THB less.
If you leave the airport in Bangkok (Suvarnabhumi), SuperRich (green and orange) and Value Plus have booths on the B floor by the Airport Rail Link.
Ask for some 100 and 500 baht notes. Taxis and small shops often cannot change 1,000 baht notes.
Changing baht back at a good changer costs little (Mamy sold USD at 33.50 on 15 Oct 2026), but don't change much more than you need.
No Thai bank holiday falls on your dates (8-18 Jan 2027): the only bank holiday in January 2027 is 1 Jan. Some Phuket Town changers close on Sundays (10 and 17 Jan).
avoid: Hotel reception exchange desks: rates are usually much worse.
Airport counters for big amounts: local guides estimate 3-5% worse than town.
Saying yes to your home currency (DCC) at an ATM or card machine: about 5% worse.
Many small ATM withdrawals: you pay 250-350 THB each time.
Bank booths when a top changer is near: on 15 Oct 2026 they paid 0.4-0.8% less for USD and about 1-1.2% less for EUR.
Street booths with a 'No commission' sign but a low rate. Compare the board with the mid-market rate first.
Strangers or Telegram accounts that offer exchange or cash delivery. Mamy says it has no Telegram account, and Money Shop names two fake Telegram accounts.
